title: Run-and-verdict simulation
statement: Let $P$ and $Q$ be deterministic machines with $k$ Boolean work tapes, let $j$ be a work tape index, and choose states $p_{\mathrm{exit}}$ of $P$ and $q_{\mathrm{entry}},q_{\mathrm{acc}},q_{\mathrm{rej}}$ of $Q$. Suppose $P$ reaches configuration $c_P$ in state $p_{\mathrm{exit}}$ for the first time after $T_P$ steps on input $z$, and tape $j$ at that configuration has a block of $m$ nonblank cells from its head position, followed by a blank, with a blank immediately to the left of the head. Let $s$ be a Boolean word of length $m$, and suppose the run of $Q$ from the configuration formed by placing $s$ on tape $j$ at the head position of $c_P$ and entering $q_{\mathrm{entry}}$ reaches $q_{\mathrm{acc}}$ or $q_{\mathrm{rej}}$ for the first time at step $T_Q$. If a choice-bit word $w$ satisfies $(w\text{ with its first }T_P+1\text{ bits removed, then truncated to }m\text{ bits})=s$ and $T_P+2m+T_Q+11\le |w|$, then running the guess-and-run machine on $w$ from its initial configuration yields a halted configuration whose input-head position and work tapes and tape-head positions are those of the stated $Q$ configuration, and whose output is that configuration's output followed by the bit indicating whether its state is $q_{\mathrm{acc}}$.
hypotheses_covered: $P,Q$ are deterministic machines with $k$ Boolean work tapes
$T_P$ is a natural number and $c_P$ is a configuration of $P$ on Boolean input $z$
$P$ run for $T_P$ steps from its initial configuration equals $c_P$
For a natural number $m$, tape $j$ has nonblank cells at offsets $p<m$ from its head
The cell at offset $m$ is blank
The cell one position left of the tape head is blank
$s$ is a Boolean word of length $m$
At time $T_Q$, the specified $Q$ run is in state $q_{\mathrm{acc}}$ or $q_{\mathrm{rej}}$
Before time $T_Q$, the specified $Q$ run has visited neither verdict state
$w$ has a segment from position $T_P+1$ through the next $m$ bits equal to $s$
